stem: Declaring a class's data members private and allowing access only through public getter and setter methods is primarily an example of which OOP concept?
explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with the methods that operate on it and hides the data from direct outside access. Private fields with public getters/setters are the textbook way to achieve this data hiding.

stem: Method overloading (several methods with the same name but different parameter lists in one class) is an example of:
explanation: With overloading, the compiler chooses which method to call from the number and types of arguments, so the binding happens at compile time. Run-time polymorphism comes from overriding a method in a subclass.
Every constructor implicitly calls its superclass constructor (super()) first. new C() calls B(), which calls A(). A() prints A, then B() finishes and prints B, then C() prints C. Output: ABC.
shortcut: Constructors run from base class to derived class

explanation: Fields are not overridden; they are resolved by the reference type. obj has type P, so obj.x is P's x = 10. Methods are dispatched on the actual object type (Q), so obj.get() runs Q.get() and returns Q's x = 20. Output: 10 20.
shortcut: Fields: reference type; instance methods: object type

explanation: run() is inherited from Base. Static methods are hidden, not overridden, so s() inside Base resolves to Base.s() = "Bs". m() is an instance method, so it dispatches to Derived.m(), which returns "Dm" + super.m() = "DmBm". Output: BsDmBm.
shortcut: Static methods bind at compile time; instance methods at run time
